definitions.meaning: to stop and gather a hit ball, as a cricketer or baseball player does
the riders who follow the hounds in a hunt are collectively called by this name

explanation.surface: A huntsman asks someone to keep hold of a ball for the people riding behind.
explanation.definitionFit: In ball games a fielder stops the ball; in foxhunting the mounted followers are known as the field.

clue.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

definitions.text: Arms displayed in a hostile way?

parts.words: Arms displayed in a hostile way?
parts.note: suggests weapons brandished, but means a posture: hands on hips with elbows jutting out, a confrontational stance

explanation.surface: Weapons being brandished threateningly.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing with hands on hips and elbows bent outwards is a defiant, aggressive pose.

indicators.note: to turn something is to twist it round, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone notes that female deer become dead miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges DOES into DESO; LATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate describes someone wretched, forlorn and unhappy.

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word for went round is dropped

parts.note: to have revolved is to have gone round in a circle

explanation.surface: Someone who has grown up went about without a shirt on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the R at the head of REVOLVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evolved has grown and changed gradually over time.

definitions.meaning: to cease or halt suddenly, as talks may be halted
the opening shot of a game of billiards or snooker that scatters the balls

explanation.surface: A player either halts or opens a frame at the billiard table.
explanation.definitionFit: To break off is to cease suddenly; the break-off is the first shot of a billiards frame.

indicators.note: a revolt overturns order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive ending gives no letter, leaving just the word boy

explanation.surface: A speaker says they will put down a lad's uprising by roundabout means.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliquely means at a slant, not straight to the point.

clue.text: Period when one is not well off

definitions.text: Period when one is not well off

parts.words: Period when one is not well off
parts.note: reads as a time of poverty, but means time off work while unwell

explanation.surface: A spell of hard times when money is short.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence from work granted because of illness is the time one is off and not well.

parts.note: sounds like a talent for lying, but means a present given to corrupt someone

explanation.surface: Someone has a natural talent for deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: An inducement handed over to influence someone corruptly is a dishonest present.

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A driver boasts about sitting in their new car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a small British motor vehicle.

definitions.meaning: the load line painted on a ship's hull, named after the MP who campaigned for it
a light canvas shoe with a rubber sole, the British name for a sneaker

explanation.surface: A famous range of shoes is in the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plimsoll line marks a ship's safe loading depth; a plimsoll is also a canvas gym shoe.

definitions.meaning: describes sloping lettering often used to stress words

explanation.surface: Someone is the sort of person who tends to speak forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic is a sloping typeface, and sloped print is used to give words emphasis.

clue.text: The first person on a Scottish isle

parts.note: the pronoun of the first person singular is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: The original settler on an island off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey.

parts.note: sounds like the end of a day's cricket, but means the closing speech of a drama

explanation.surface: Stumps are drawn at the end of the day's cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A short concluding speech or section at the end of a drama or book.

parts.note: when making a call, being put through means the line is joined to the other party

explanation.surface: Someone got somewhere by making phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: On the phone, being through means the call is linked to the person dialled.

parts.note: sounds like a vessel travelling overland, but means one sailing close to the shore

explanation.surface: A boat that somehow travels over dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel trading between ports along the shoreline stays near the land.

clue.text: I've only a piece of material around me so trembled with cold

indicators.note: the scrap of cloth is placed around the words before, enclosing them

parts.note: a shred is a scrap or strip torn from cloth
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A scantily dressed person explains why they shook in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts IVE inside SHRED, after SH; 'only' and 'me' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is to shake involuntarily, as when chilled.

clue.text: Kind of shirt with a frill very tasteful

parts.note: the T-shirt gives the letter T
a ruffle is a gathered frill of fabric

explanation.surface: A style of shirt with frilled trim looks very elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteful' here means full of taste, delicious, not refined.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus prized by gourmets, or a rich chocolate sweet, is highly flavoursome.

parts.note: the first of two women's names is Rose
the second of two women's names is Mary

explanation.surface: Two women who never seem to age.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic shrub that keeps its leaves all year.

parts.note: suggests a strange-looking ogre, but singular means having one eye to look with

explanation.surface: An odd-looking huge person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Cyclops was a one-eyed giant.

indicators.note: something blown apart is scattered, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: The whole of eternity has been destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety is the total, everything together.

indicators.note: something misshapen is out of form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A crooked nose makes someone look older.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long periods of time.

definitions.meaning: to slide or swing round out of control
the past tense of slay, to kill

explanation.surface: A car's slide led to a fatality.
explanation.definitionFit: To slew is to swerve or slide sideways; it is also the past of slay, meaning killed.

clue.text: Game in the form of a puzzle

indicators.note: putting letters in another form reshapes them into a new order

explanation.surface: A game shaped like a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link: 'the form of' rearranges GAMEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery that is hard to work out.

indicators.note: putting things in order arranges them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales representative might win a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep is a representative acting on someone's behalf, such as a sales agent.

definitions.meaning: to shield or hide from view
to show a film or programme to an audience

explanation.surface: A choice between hiding something and putting it on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen hides things behind it; screening a film is showing it publicly.

clue.text: They periodically take a self sacrificing journey to the sea

definitions.text: They periodically take a self sacrificing journey to the sea

parts.words: They periodically take a self sacrificing journey to the sea
parts.note: describes the popular legend of Arctic rodents rushing in droves to drown

explanation.surface: Some group regularly makes a selfless trip to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Arctic rodents are popularly believed to hurl themselves off cliffs during mass migrations.

clue.text: Having no inclination for a palindrome

definitions.meaning: a word reading the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: Someone has no desire to write words that read both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat has no slope; the word itself reads the same in either direction.

clue.text: Possibly meant to go round some accommodation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around a word, enclosing it
suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters that follow

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone intended to look round a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns MEANT into AMENT, which 'to go round' wraps around PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms to live in.
